newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rate rises on weekend covering.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rate rises on weekend covering.

text.p: * Volume heavy at 26.627 bln from 11.412 bln pesos
Philippine interbank call loan rates edged up on Monday to an average of 11.625 from 11.0625 percent as banks borrowed more money to cover their weekend positions, traders said.
"Short-term positions tightened because banks were covering four days," said a dealer, since Friday was a holiday.
Rates hit a day-high of 12.75 percent, while the low was at 11.0625.
Out of the 65 participating financial institutions, 37 were lenders.
In the secondary market for T-bills, dealers said activity was muted since banks concentrated on correcting their reserve positions for the four days.
Moroever, banks wanted to see the results of the day's primary auction for T-bills later in the day, they said.
One dealer said the three-month bill was quoted an offer rate of 11.55 percent; six months at 11.95; and the one year at 12.50.
